chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who divorces his wife with a single divorce during a period of purity without sexual intercourse, and leaves her until she enters her third menstrual cycle and her bath (for the third period) arrives, then he revokes her and bears witness to his revocation, he said: 'He has more right to her as long as she has not become permissible for marriage to another.'

key_terms.أَمْلَكُ بِهَا: he has more right to her
key_terms.تَحِلَّ لَهَا: she becomes permissible (for marriage to another)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on revoking a single divorce if it occurred during a period of purity without sexual intercourse?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific conditions for *raj'ah* (revocable divorce) when the marriage has not yet been consummated, emphasizing that the waiting period (*iddah*) is determined by menstrual cycles rather than pregnancy. It highlights the juristic principle that the husband retains exclusive authority over the marital bond until the wife becomes fully free (*halal*) for another suitor, a key distinction in Shia fiqh regarding the finality of the first divorce.
